headline: Amazonia Review of Mirror Complains It 'Shows the Wrong Person'
subheadline: One-star review goes viral; support team reportedly 'escalated to leadership'
summary: A product review claiming a mirror reflects 'someone else' has accumulated 50,000 'helpful' votes and no resolution.
content:
An Amazonia review of a standard wall mirror has gone viral after the purchaser complained that the product "shows the wrong person."

The one-star review, posted by verified purchaser "J. Thompson," reads in its entirety:

"One star. Mirror arrived undamaged but clearly defective. When I look into it, I see someone who looks tired and older than I remember being. This is not accurate. I am younger and more vibrant than whatever this mirror is showing. Requested refund but was told 'that's just how mirrors work.' Unacceptable. I've seen myself before and this isn't it. The mirror is showing someone else's reflection, possibly a tired relative. Please advise."

The review has received 50,000 "helpful" votes, the most of any product review in Amazonia history. Comments are disabled, but the Q&A section has accumulated 847 questions, most asking variations of "have you tried looking at a different angle" and "are you okay."

Amazonia's customer service initially responded with standard troubleshooting: "Have you tried cleaning the mirror? Is there adequate lighting?" J. Thompson replied: "The lighting is fine. The problem is that the reflection is of someone who has clearly given up on several life goals. That's not me. I still have goals."

A follow-up response from Amazonia read: "We're sorry to hear this. We've escalated your case to leadership." There has been no further communication.

The review has prompted philosophical discussions about self-perception and the passage of time. It has also prompted a surge in mirror returns, with several customers citing "similar defects."

"I also got a defective one," wrote one reviewer. "Mine shows someone who should really get more sleep. Clearly a manufacturing batch issue."

At press time, J. Thompson had ordered a second mirror. Their review: "Same problem. Beginning to suspect this is intentional."
author: Alex Rivera, Digital Culture
